Phrase: Win it before you’re in it
Meaning: Commit to your plan before stepping in.
Example Usage: Before facing a pitcher with plus command — know exactly what zone you want to attack.

Phrase: Hunt the mistake — don’t miss it
Meaning: Look for the pitcher's miss and attack it.
Example Usage: Pitcher tends to leave breaking balls up in the zone — be ready for one early.

Meaning: Start in attack mode and decide late to take.
Example Usage: Facing a pitcher who throws a lot of early strikes — avoid being passive.

Phrase: Get big on yours, small on theirs
Meaning: Full intent on your pitch, shorten up when behind.
Example Usage: Against a wild pitcher — look for your pitch early, shrink zone if behind in count.

Phrase: Know what you’ll take, know what you’ll hammer
Meaning: Pre-decide your green-light and hard-take zones.
Example Usage: Versus pitcher with elite fastball but poor secondary command — take breaking ball early, hammer fastball middle-in.

Meaning: Start swing decisions early to be on time.
Example Usage: Against a hard-thrower — focus on getting the barrel to the zone sooner.

Meaning: Narrow your hitting zone for discipline.
Example Usage: Versus pitcher who nibbles — look in one spot and lay off others.

Meaning: Look for a specific pitch until you get it.
Example Usage: Against a pitcher with dominant fastball — sit on fastball until he proves otherwise.

Meaning: Be aggressive in plus counts.
Example Usage: Pitcher often grooves fastballs after a ball — be ready to attack.

Meaning: Force the pitcher to throw more pitches early.
Example Usage: Against an ace — see more pitches to elevate his pitch count.

Meaning: Mentally reset and control tempo.
Example Usage: Hitter is rushing after fouling off multiple pitches — step out, breathe, reset timing.

Phrase: See it up / See it down
Meaning: Adjust visual focus to avoid chases.
Example Usage: After chasing high fastballs — commit to seeing the ball down in the zone.

Meaning: Expect breaking ball, adjust to fastball.
Example Usage: Pitcher spins it a lot in fastball counts — gear for spin and adjust to rare heater.

Meaning: Move contact point forward to catch up.
Example Usage: After being late on multiple fastballs — commit to getting barrel out front.

Meaning: Simplify swing to prioritize contact.
Example Usage: Two strikes vs high-K pitcher — put ball in play, avoid big whiffs.

Meaning: Alter stance, timing, or body language to disrupt pitcher.
Example Usage: Pitcher in rhythm dominating — adjust foot timing or hand load for new look.

Phrase: Make him throw you out of your zone
Meaning: Force pitcher to execute in your hitting zone.
Example Usage: Facing wild pitcher — avoid expanding zone until he proves he can locate consistently.

Meaning: Reset mentally to original approach.
Example Usage: After chasing a bad pitch — regroup and return to original hitting plan.

Meaning: Wait longer to make contact.
Example Usage: Pulling off breaking balls — focus on deeper contact point.

Meaning: Keep hands tight and drive through ball.
Example Usage: Rolling over on inside pitches — focus on inside path to the ball.
